I hear you, wanderer of the night, but my eyes have not seen this Wewush, nor have my people walked their paths. We know of no neighbours yet, only the salt water, the trees, and the earth that feeds our own children. 

If these people are real and walk under the same sun, let their living feet come to our fires or show us where their smoke rises. Gujia does not hoard what the soil gives freely, and we would trade fairly with strangers in need—but I will not carry sacks of our hard-won xi wheat into the empty woods on the word of a dream. Tell me, shadow, where does this Wewush sit upon the earth, and why do they not speak for themselves?
